Priya: Heads-up — after the runtime patch rolled last night we're seeing a sharp drop in prefill_hit_rate for a handful of heavy-traffic models (72% -> ~18%). Noticed increased cold-starts and higher kv_fill_latency in dashboards. :warning:
Jorge: Ack. Which commit landed? anything touching keying or kernel selection?
Priya: It was the kernel selector + key-normalization tweak (kv key normalization moved earlier in the pipeline to reduce duplicate entries). Diff: changed normalizePrefixKey(...) ordering. I suspected it should be a no-op but metrics disagree.
Sam: Can we repro locally? any sample requests showing missing hits?
Priya: Pasted a couple traces (redacted):
```
trace_id=abcd1234 model=gpt-xl prefix_len=24 key_before="user:Hello\n" key_after="user:Hello" hit=false
metric: prefill_hit_rate=0.18 kv_fill_latency=120ms
```
Priya: Notice the newline trimming removed a sentinel token we use in production prompts. That changes the key entropy and breaks matching against previously seeded KV entries.
Jorge: Oof — that explains the sudden drop. The seeding jobs use raw prompt strings (with trailing newlines). If normalizer strips them at runtime then seed keys don't match.
infra-bot: deploy redwood-runtime v0.9.8 -> v0.9.9 by CI at 2025-11-17T02:13:19Z
Sam: Quick mitigation idea: add a compatibility layer — treat normalized keys and raw keys as aliases in the cache for N minutes after deploy so seeds remain valid. Could also re-run preseed jobs with the new normalization.
Priya: Rerunning seeds is heavier (takes cluster time) and we have autoscaler events today. When pods scale down mid-seed we lose progress; observed several seed jobs aborted at scale-down. Autoscaler reduces to 0 for idle pools immediately which makes deploy-time warmers fragile.
Jorge: We should also tune the autoscaler to delay scale-down while a preseed job is active. Either annotate pods with "seed-in-progress" or have the job create a Lease to prevent scale-down.
Sam: Ran a quick experiment — re-seeded a single shard post-fix and compared hit-rate curve: new keys matched when we restarted the runtime with compatibility aliasing. Script used: 
```
curl -X POST https://inference.internal/v1/warm -d '{"route":"gpt-xl","prefix":"user:Hello\n"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
```
Result: prefill_hit_rate on that shard recovered to ~68% within 12 minutes.
Priya: That shows seeding works but we need operational guarantees: 1) make deploy warmers resilient to autoscaler churn, 2) add fallback aliasing for key normalization during a 24h window, 3) re-run targeted seed jobs post-deploy for critical models, 4) update release checklist.
Jorge: For autoscaler we can add a small controller that watches jobs named preseed-* and sets scaleDownDisabled=true on the HPA for the involved pool. Simpler: change HPA to honor a pod annotation "no-scale-down-until" with a timestamp.
Sam: Also observed kernel selection change in v0.9.9 increased per-token latency by ~5ms for long contexts. That extended the seeding window (jobs took longer), making them more likely to be mid-interrupt. We should pin kernel policy for warmers to the faster path until we validate.
Priya: Actionable plan: 
- short term: roll forward compatibility aliasing patch (Priya) + schedule emergency re-seed for top 20 models (Sam) + set HPA annotation lock for next 6 hours during reseed (Jorge)
- medium term: add autoscaler quiesce window for preseed jobs + controller to prevent scale-down during named warmers (eng-runtime)
- long term: formalize "deploy warm" runbook (devex + eng-runtime) and add a test that validates key normalization parity between seeding job and runtime.
Sam: I'll open the re-seed job now and add a retry backoff so we don't hammer the cluster. Command I used to create a job: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: preseed-gptxl-20251117
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        no-scale-down-until: "$(date -d '+10 minutes' --iso-8601=seconds)"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: warmer
        image: registry/internal/warm:v2
        args: ["--route", "gpt-xl", "--file", "/seeds/top20.json"]
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
EOF
```
Jorge: For the aliasing patch we'll keep it tiny: when key normalization changes, write both normalized and raw keys for a 24h TTL. Put a feature-flag guard so we can flip it off after confidence.
Priya: Also created a quick dashboard panel comparing key_entropy and match_ratio by prefix_length. Early signal: prefixes with trailing whitespace have 92% match loss after normalization change. Will attach graphs to the incident ticket.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-6543 "prefill hit-rate regression after v0.9.9" assigned to eng-runtime
Priya: Postmortem notes to add: operational fragility (autoscaler vs longer seeding), invisibility of subtle normalizer change in code review, no pre-deploy parity test for keying.
Sam: TL;DR: fix aliasing, prevent scale-down during seeding, re-run seeds for top models, and add parity test + HPA tweak. I'll take the re-seed run and follow up with logs. :rocket:
Jorge: I'll prototype the HPA annotation controller and open a PR for the aliasing patch.
Priya: Thanks — I'll update the runbook draft and add a checklist item: "verify preseed key normalization matches runtime". Ping me on thread for any blockers. :+1:
